chunks: Aban narrated from Jamil, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

If the claimant presents evidence, then no oath is upon him. But if he does not present evidence, and the one against whom the claim was made refers the oath back to him, and he refuses, then he has no right.

key_terms.ادُّعِيَ عَلَيْهِ: the one against whom the claim is made, the defendant
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: clear evidence or proof establishing the claim
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: the claimant who brings a legal claim
key_terms.حَقَّ: a legally recognized right or valid claim
key_terms.يَمِينٌ: a legal oath used in judicial procedure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a claimant has no evidence and refuses the oath in an Islamic legal dispute?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning claims and oaths in adjudication. If the claimant establishes proof, no oath is required from him; but if he lacks evidence and refuses the returned oath, his claim is no longer upheld.
